title: Whole-Body Contact-Rich Compliant Motion Planning Based on Morphology Representation
content: Robots operating in daily environments, such as householdorganization and object manipu lation, often encounter densely cluttered spaces where collision-free motion is infeasible. To safely and effectively interact with surrounding objects, robots require task-agnostic whole body contact-rich motion planning that can handle time-varying multi-contact interactions. However, model-based approaches are limited by the difficulty of accurately estimating unknown interaction dynamics online, while learning-based approaches typically rely on task-specific demonstrations or reward functions, restricting their generalization to unseen tasks.This paper proposes a physics-model-guided whole-body contact-rich motion planning framework based on material-point morphology representation and interaction motion prediction supervision. The robot body is represented by a set of material points with consistent body correspondence, enabling unified encoding of whole-body motion and tactile interaction states under varying contact locations, contact configurations, and force distributions. Furthermore, interaction motion prediction generated from a tactile-driven interaction planner is used as physical supervision to train MorphoPlanner, an end-to-end motion morphology planning network that generates future whole-body motion references from task objectives and current interaction states without requiring task-specific demonstrations or manually designed rewards. A whole-body tactile interaction dataset containing 749K samples is constructed for model training and evaluation. Extensive experiments, including compliant interaction tests, stress tests in highly cluttered environments, and comparisons with representative planning methods, are conducted on simulation and real-world dual-arm tactile platforms. The proposed framework achieves success rates of 95.5%-100% in dense cluttered scenarios and demonstrates stable whole-body contact-rich motion generation under real-world physical interactions. These results validate the effectiveness of the proposed morphology-aware planning framework for improving robot adaptability in unknown and cluttered environments.
